Assess the case-dropping stability of the edge weights

Source: R/casedrop_reliability_htna.R
casedrop_reliability_htna.Rd

casedrop_reliability_htna() measures how far the estimated edge weights of an htna network depend on a few sessions, by case-dropping stability (Epskamp et al., 2018). Networks are re-estimated after dropping increasing proportions of the sessions, and the edge weights of each reduced network are correlated with those of the full network. The case-dropping stability (CS) coefficient is the largest proportion of sessions that can be dropped while the correlation stays above a threshold (0.7 by default) in a required share (95 percent) of the resamples; Epskamp et al. (2018) recommend a coefficient of at least 0.25 and preferably above 0.5.

casedrop_reliability_htna() applies the procedure to the edge-weight vector of an htna network, or to every cohort of a grouped network, and also reports the mean and maximum absolute weight differences at each drop proportion. It runs Nestimate's casedrop_reliability() on the network and returns a net_casedrop_reliability object (a net_casedrop_reliability_group for a grouped network).

For the stability of node centralities use centrality_stability_htna(); for split-half agreement use reliability_htna(); for edge-level confidence intervals use bootstrap_htna().

Usage

casedrop_reliability_htna(x, ...)

Arguments

x

An htna network from build_htna() or an htna_group.

...

Settings: iter (resamples per drop proportion, default 1000), drop_prop (default seq(0.1, 0.9, by = 0.1)), threshold (0.7), certainty (0.95), method (correlation, "spearman"), include_diag (FALSE), seed, target (the edges assessed: "auto", "existing" or "all"; Nestimate 1.0.2 or later) and actor (drop whole actors instead of sessions; Nestimate 1.0.19 or later).

Value

An object of class net_casedrop_reliability (one network) or net_casedrop_reliability_group (a grouped network), with print(), summary() and plot() methods; summary() returns a data frame with one row per metric and drop proportion (columns metric, drop_prop, mean, sd, median, mad, q025, q975).

References

Epskamp, S., Borsboom, D., & Fried, E. I. (2018). Estimating psychological networks and their accuracy: A tutorial paper. Behavior Research Methods, 50(1), 195-212. doi:10.3758/s13428-017-0862-1

See also

centrality_stability_htna(), reliability_htna(), bootstrap_htna().

Examples

data(human_ai)
net <- build_htna(human_ai, actor_type = "actor_type")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (1 sessions), 'cluster' (42 sessions), 'actor_type' (24 sessions)
casedrop_reliability_htna(net, iter = 20, seed = 1)
#> Edge-weight Case-dropping Stability
#>   Cases (resampled)     : 429
#>   Edges assessed        : 125 (diagonal excluded)
#>   Iterations / prop     : 20
#>   Correlation method    : spearman
#>   CS-coefficient (r)    : 0.90  (threshold=0.70, certainty=0.95)
#> 
#> Model-level reliability across iterations (mean +/- sd per drop):
#>   drop_prop      p=0.1        p=0.2        p=0.3        p=0.4        p=0.5        p=0.6        p=0.7        p=0.8        p=0.9      
#>   mean|diff|      0.002+- 0.000   0.003+- 0.000   0.004+- 0.000   0.006+- 0.001   0.007+- 0.001   0.008+- 0.001   0.010+- 0.001   0.014+- 0.002   0.020+- 0.003
#>   median|diff|    0.001+- 0.000   0.002+- 0.000   0.003+- 0.000   0.004+- 0.000   0.004+- 0.000   0.005+- 0.001   0.006+- 0.001   0.008+- 0.001   0.013+- 0.002
#>   cor             0.998+- 0.001   0.996+- 0.001   0.995+- 0.001   0.991+- 0.002   0.987+- 0.003   0.982+- 0.005   0.973+- 0.005   0.958+- 0.008   0.919+- 0.021
#>   max|diff|       0.016+- 0.006   0.024+- 0.008   0.028+- 0.009   0.039+- 0.017   0.052+- 0.016   0.059+- 0.018   0.076+- 0.021   0.101+- 0.039   0.118+- 0.028
